role.io: An input or output of the network rather than a layer: what goes in, what comes back out. Nothing is learned here.
role.embed: A projection that turns raw inputs into vectors the network can work with, or maps between two granularities (atoms and tokens, pixels and patches). Mostly linear layers and lookup tables; cheap next to the stacks that follow.
role.attn: An attention layer. Every position builds a query, compares it with the keys of the positions it is allowed to see, and takes a weighted sum of their values. This is how information moves between distant parts of the input; which positions may attend to which is what distinguishes global, windowed and distance-gated variants.
role.mlp: A position-wise feed-forward layer: the same small network applied independently at every position, widening to an inner dimension and back. Attention moves information between positions; this transforms it in place, and usually holds most of the parameters.
role.norm: A normalisation or modulation layer. It rescales activations to keep training stable, and in diffusion models it is also where the conditioning enters: the scale and shift are predicted from the noise level and the condition instead of being learned constants (FiLM, AdaLN).
role.conv: A convolution or residual block. It mixes a position with its spatial neighbours using shared weights, so it is naturally translation-equivariant and cheap on grids. The building block of U-Net denoisers.
role.cond: The conditioning path: where everything the denoiser is told about the target enters, and where the noise level is embedded. In a co-folding model this is also the boundary between the part computed once per target and the part recomputed at every step.
role.latent: An autoencoder stage. The diffusion process does not run on the data itself but on a compressed latent, with an encoder in front and a decoder behind, so the denoiser works at a much smaller resolution.
role.pair: A pair representation: one vector per pair of tokens, holding what the network believes about the relationship between them — typically distance and orientation. It is quadratic in sequence length, which is why it dominates the cost of a folding trunk.

key.noise: The starting point of the reverse process: pure Gaussian noise at the largest noise level of the schedule. Each sample begins from a different draw, which is the only source of diversity between samples of the same target.
key.xhat: The denoiser's estimate of the clean data given the current noisy state. The sampler does not jump to it; it takes a step toward it, re-noises a little, and asks again.
key.cond: Where the condition and the noise level are injected. The noise level is turned into a vector by a Fourier or sinusoidal embedding and added to the condition, so one network can serve every noise level instead of one network per step.
key.aenc: The atom encoder. It attends over atoms — only locally, since atoms far apart in the structure have little to say to each other — and then pools each token's atoms into a single token vector, handing a much shorter sequence to the transformer above.
key.tok: The token transformer: the main body of the denoiser, attending globally over tokens. The condition enters here twice over, as AdaLN scales and shifts from the single representation and as a learned bias added to every attention logit from the pair representation.
key.adec: The atom decoder. It broadcasts the token features back down to the atoms they came from and runs local attention again, ending in a linear layer that outputs a coordinate update per atom.
key.c: The condition handed to the denoiser. It is computed once per target and reused for every sampling step and every sample, which is why the trunk is expensive but amortised, while the denoiser is cheap but paid for hundreds of times.
key.pf: The Pairformer: the folding trunk's main stack, alternating triangle updates on the pair representation with attention on the single representation. Triangle updates enforce a geometric consistency — if i is close to k and k to j, that constrains i and j — which is what makes the stack expensive and what the lighter models drop.
key.msa: The MSA module. A multiple sequence alignment holds evolutionary cousins of the input sequence; positions that mutate together are usually in contact, and this module distils that signal into the pair representation.
key.tmpl: The template module. Known structures of related proteins are embedded as pair features and averaged into the pair representation, giving the trunk a structural prior.
key.conf: The confidence head. It does not change the structure; it predicts how much to trust it, per atom and per pair, and its scores are what rank several samples of the same target against each other.
key.emb: The input embedder: raw inputs become the single and pair representations the trunk works with, including the relative-position and bond features that tell the network how the tokens are connected.
key.input: What the user supplies. Everything downstream is a function of this plus the noise draw, so what can be asked of the model is set here.
key.out: What comes back, after any ranking or post-processing that is not part of the network.
key.ipa: Invariant point attention, the layer AlphaFold 2's structure module is built from. Each residue carries a rigid frame; besides ordinary query-key attention, every head places a few query and key points in 3D using the residue's frame, and the distance between those points enters the attention logit. Rotating the whole structure rotates the points with it, so the output does not change.
key.score: The network's output for a score model: an estimate of the gradient of the log-density of the noised data, here per residue and in that residue's own frame. A solver turns it into the next, less noisy state; it is not a clean structure itself.
key.pairmixer: A PairMixer block: triangle multiplication (outgoing, then incoming) and a transition on the pair representation, nothing else. No triangle attention and no attention on the single representation, which is what makes it cheaper than a Pairformer block.
key.coup: A coupling step between two residual streams that run at different granularities. Token features are broadcast to their atoms and mixed into the atom stream; the features of each token's centre atom are mixed back into the token stream. Both mixes are MLPs gated by the conditioning.
key.readout: The output layer: token and atom features are projected to a common width, added per atom, normalised and mapped to a three-dimensional coordinate update.
key.mid: The middle of a U-Net, at the lowest resolution and the widest channels. Attention is affordable here, so this is where the most global reasoning happens.
